checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan CI rollback: remove the GitHub Actions matrix and badge because hosted runners cannot start on this account; keep CHANGELOG and local test command

impact_assessment.why: The workflow is valid but every job is refused before startup by an account billing lock, leaving a red badge and failed checks on every push
impact_assessment.benefits: Repository checks stay meaningful and the release history remains; no misleading CI signal
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: removes GitHub Actions only; concurrency: none; state: README/changelog/tree
impact_assessment.mitigation: Delete the workflow and badge, update the tree and Unreleased notes, run all gates

checkpoints.description: [2/2] CI rollback complete: unavailable workflow and badge removed, changelog kept; 174 tests, 4/4 gates; checklists: passed

handoff.evidence: 174 tests OK, README tree passes guidelines

[1/3] Plan selective reruns: --force NAME with --resume rerenders chosen accepted tracks, preserves other state, and previews 'forced' in dry-run

impact_assessment.why: A track can be accepted but still unsatisfactory, or need a new take after a model change; currently the only way to rerender it is to delete state or rerun the whole manifest
impact_assessment.benefits: One named track can be regenerated while every other accepted track stays reused, with a dry-run preview and unchanged manifest fingerprint
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --force flag; dependency: none added; concurrency: sequential batch; state: only forced entries are replaced
impact_assessment.mitigation: Case-insensitive exact labels, reject unknown names and --force without --resume before any write, include forced tracks in render_required, test state preservation and dry-run

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Forced reruns complete: 178 tests, 4/4 gates; force rerendered one accepted track, unknown/without-resume rejected, dry-run marked forced; checklists: passed

handoff.next: commit and push the force-rerun release

[1/4] Plan muse doctor: read-only checks for Python, output writability, provider/judge names and required keys, human/JSON output and tests

impact_assessment.why: Users discover bad configuration only when a generate or batch command fails, often after setup; there is no single command that explains what is configured and what is missing
impact_assessment.benefits: One read-only command shows the Python version, output path, adapter names and key presence with Fix lines, using no network or provider calls
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new doctor command; dependency: none added; concurrency: read-only; state: no directories or files written
impact_assessment.mitigation: Check the nearest existing output ancestor instead of creating it, never print key values, catch configuration errors as findings, and test every fail branch

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Doctor complete: 187 tests, 4/4 gates; healthy, missing-key, override, output-file and invalid-config paths tested and dogfooded; checklists: passed

handoff.next: commit and push the doctor release

[1/3] Plan catalog paging semantics: total counts every match, shown counts the limited result, and human/JSON output state both

impact_assessment.why: muse list --limit returns total equal to the limited rows, so JSON consumers cannot tell whether more artifacts matched or how many were withheld
impact_assessment.benefits: Callers can page accurately and users see 'shown of total' instead of a misleading count
impact_assessment.risks: contract: JSON total/added shown fields; dependency: none; concurrency: read-only; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Load/filter/sort all matches, slice only at the CLI, keep the library limit parameter, update tests and docs

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Catalog total semantics complete: 187 tests, 4/4 gates; limit 1 on 2 matches reports total 2, shown 1; checklists: passed

handoff.next: commit and push the paging fix

[1/3] Plan generate dry-run: validate prompt/theme/duration/attempts and print provider/judge/output with no calls, artifacts or key checks

impact_assessment.why: Batch has a cost-free plan, but a single generate run still requires invoking the pipeline just to inspect the resolved request and settings
impact_assessment.benefits: Single-track automation can validate inputs and show the exact plan before spending, with the same zero-call guarantee as batch dry-run
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --dry-run flag on generate; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no output or metadata
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build MusicRequest first so invalid input still exits 2, return before compose, test counting provider and no output directory
